findings.title: Exit-code contract changed: 4 now means "feature disabled" instead of "recreate required"
findings.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was changed from 4 to 3 and 4 is reused for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. Any consumer written against the previously released behaviour of the `update-compatibility check` command (automation/DevOps pipelines, as explicitly encouraged by the guide, and the Operator's auto-update logic that inspects the Job's exit code) will now mis-interpret results: a check that tested `exit == 4` for "recreate needed" will now trigger a downtime upgrade when the only problem is that the preview feature is not enabled, and will not recognise exit code 3 at all. The reverse mapping is just as harmful: code expecting 3 to be unused will now receive it for the common recreate case. Since both codes are swapped in the same release, consumers must be updated in lockstep (operator source is not touched in this PR) and the change should be called out in release notes / upgrade notes.

findings.title: New/changed exit codes are not asserted by any test
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr message and only for the `metadata` sub-command; it never asserts that the process exits with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (4), and the `check` sub-command is not covered at all. Likewise `testWrongVersions` asserts only the error text, not the new `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` (3). Because the exit codes are the documented, scriptable contract of this command (and were just renumbered from 4 to 3), a regression in either value would pass CI unnoticed. Add assertions on `result.exitCode()` for the feature-disabled case (both sub-commands) and for the incompatible-version case.

findings.title: Documented command appends --features=rolling-updates, silently replacing the user's feature set
findings.body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now renders `bin/kc.[sh|bat] update-compatibility <params> --features=rolling-updates`. `--features` is a list option that replaces, not extends, the configured feature set, so a deployment that runs with e.g. `--features=admin-fine-grained-authz` will be analysed with a different feature configuration than the running server. This directly contradicts the warning in update-compatibility.adoc ("Ensure that all configuration options ... are included ... Omitting any configuration options will result in incomplete metadata") and can yield a wrong rolling/recreate verdict. The docs should instead instruct the user to add `rolling-updates` to their existing `--features` value. The same rendered command also breaks for pre-built/optimized distributions, where passing the build-time `--features` option together with `--optimized` is rejected.

findings.title: CR-only instructions for enabling rolling-updates are incomplete for custom/optimized images
findings.body: The new CAUTION and the example tell users to enable the preview feature only via `spec.features.enabled: [rolling-updates]`. For deployments using a custom image (`spec.image`), the Operator starts the server with `--optimized`, so build-time options such as `features` must already be baked into the image - exactly what this PR does for the test image in `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image` (`kc.sh build ... --features=rolling-updates`). Without mentioning this, users of custom images will either see the server reject the build-time option or run without the feature while believing it is enabled. The CAUTION also does not say how the Operator "will fail", which makes it hard to diagnose.

findings.title: New feature enum requires regenerating CLI help/doc snapshots
findings.body: `ROLLING_UPDATES` is added to `Profile.Feature`, which feeds the `--features` option's enumerated "Possible values" text in the CLI help and the generated configuration documentation. The approved help output files under `quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/resources/help/` (compared verbatim by the help dist tests) are not updated in this PR, so those tests will fail or the documented feature list will be stale. Regenerate the approved help output after adding the feature.

findings.title: setEnabledFeatures overwrites any features already configured in the test deployment
findings.body: `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))` replaces the whole list. The preceding null check on `getFeatureSpec()` implies the base deployment produced by `getTestKeycloakDeployment(true)` may already carry a FeatureSpec with enabled features; those would be silently dropped, changing what the test actually exercises (and potentially breaking the test if a required feature is removed). Append to the existing list instead of overwriting it.
